Exhibit 8: Loss and Defense and Cost Containment (DCCE) Trend 
The standard exhibit has been completed for all perils combined. For HO-3 and HO-5, we felt it 
was the most appropriate to select the 12-point trend because it uses more of our data and fits the 
data well. In addition, changing the trending period would impact the premium trend. Evaluating 
all the combinations of frequency, severity, and premium trend to get a loss ratio trend for HO-3 
and HO-5 (where frequency is closed, severity is paid), we get this table of trends: 
 
8-point 
1.33 
12-point 
1.09 
16-point 
1.05 
20-point 
1.05 
24-point 
1.11 
 
Thus, the 12-point trend selection also results in the median loss ratio trend that could be 
selected. Previously, we also selected the 12-point trend, however we had instead selected the 
frequency reported. If we instead selected the reported, our loss trend would have been 5.8% 
instead of the 5.1% that was selected.  
 
For MH-7, we thought stability of the book was reasonable and a 20 point trend is consistent 
with past experience.   
 
 
 
 
Exhibit 9: Catastrophe Adjustment 
25 years of internal Homeowners loss experience in California was used to determine a 
catastrophe load by splitting incurred losses into catastrophic and non-catastrophic components.
